answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a bonded stake: each agent locks a scarce quartz deposit to claim one identity and receive work. The protocol treats that locked deposit as the kernel of trust, paying rewards only to bonded agents and slashing the entire bond on detected fraud. To impersonate a thousand agents, an attacker must lock a thousand separate quartz stakes, so the upfront cost and forfeiture risk scale linearly with every fake identity. Even a willow-thin margin per fake cannot repay that capital, making mass impersonation economically irrational.
